claude.sample_unit: ECG segments (10-second ICU segments from 226 patients, expert-annotated test set)
models_evaluated: ECG-FM (open-source transformer ECG foundation model, MIMIC-IV-ECG fine-tuned public version)
ECG-FM fine-tuned on PTB-XL and Chapman-Shaoxing
ECG-FM fine-tuned on public data plus Amsterdam UMC-weak data

links.outcome: Off-the-shelf vs locally fine-tuned ECG-FM performance on local expert-labelled ICU data
links.effect: Off-the-shelf model F1 0.523 (AF) and 0.677 (SR) on Amsterdam UMC Expert; after fine-tuning F1 0.814/0.914 (public only) and 0.830/0.920 (with local weak data).
links.quote: Evaluation of publicly released ECG-FM in Experiment 2 on the Amsterdam UMC dataset demonstrated limited generalisation.

links.outcome: Effect of local fine-tuning with in-house ICU data on performance
links.effect: Adding Amsterdam UMC-weak data raised AF F1 on the Amsterdam UMC-weak test set from 0.743 to 0.829 and SR from 0.957 to 0.970; on Expert set AF 0.814 to 0.830, SR 0.914 to 0.920.
links.quote: After incorporating in-house data, the largest performance gains appeared on the Amsterdam UMC-weak test set, where F1 scores increased from 0.743 to 0.829 (AF) and from 0.957 to 0.970 (SR), indicating that institution-specific weak labels can enhance performance on noisy datasets.

links.outcome: Label quality of nurse weak labels versus expert-adjudicated reference standard
links.effect: Nurse-assigned labels had PPV 0.91 for AF and 0.77 for SR against clinician annotations; pairwise kappa median 0.60 for SR and 0.49 for AF between annotators.
links.quote: In addition, we evaluated the Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of nurse-assigned labels against clinician-annotated rhythm labels, obtaining a PPV of 0.91 for AF and 0.77 for SR (see Appendix Fig. 7 ).

links.outcome: Performance drop from development data to ICU deployment population
links.effect: Public model fine-tuned on MIMIC-IV-ECG gave AF precision 0.359 and F1 0.523, SR F1 0.677 on ICU expert data, showing dataset shift.
links.quote: Off-the-shelf model showed limited transferability (F1 = 0.68 for sinus rhythm (SR), 0.52 for atrial fibrillation (AF)).

links.outcome: Model performance stratified by sex and age subgroups
links.effect: Minimal differences between sexes and greater variability across age groups for AF than SR, attributed to small uneven subgroup sizes rather than genuine bias.
links.quote: Demographic analyses showed minimal differences between sexes and greater variability across age groups for AF than for SR, again likely reflecting uneven and small subgroup sizes rather than genuine model bias (Figure 5 ) [ 35 ].

links.outcome: Robustness to varying lead configurations, noisy segments and temporal windows
links.effect: Performance stable across 5-10s windows and broadly consistent across lead combinations; lower performance on noisy-but-interpretable segments than clean ones.
links.quote: Performance was stable across temporal windows, with slightly greater–but still modest–variability across lead configurations, likely influenced by the imbalance between the 1–4 and 5–8 lead groups (Appendix Tables 13 – 14 ).

links.outcome: Label consistency and performance variation across public datasets/sites
links.effect: Within-dataset F1 varied by source: SR F1 0.989 Chapman-Shaoxing, 0.971 PTB-XL, 0.799 Georgia, 0.651 CPSC; AF F1 0.756 Georgia vs 0.944 Chapman-Shaoxing.
links.quote: In contrast, Georgia and CPSC showed weaker and more variable performance, particularly for SR (Table 1 ), suggesting annotation inconsistencies or distribution shifts.

links.outcome: Dataset documentation completeness and its relation to label consistency
links.effect: Georgia dataset lacked formal procedural documentation and showed weaker label consistency; well-documented PTB-XL and Chapman-Shaoxing showed stronger consistency.
links.quote: In contrast, the Georgia dataset lacks formal procedural documentation entirely, providing only its geographical origin.

unlisted_practices: Curating fine-tuning datasets by assessing internal label consistency (using within-dataset classifier performance as proxy) before selection
Weak-supervision augmentation of training data with routine nurse-charted labels

models_evaluated: ECG-FM fine-tuned on PTB-XL and Chapman-Shaoxing
ECG-FM fine-tuned on PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, and Amsterdam UMC-weak

links.outcome: local ICU rhythm classification performance
links.effect: Off-the-shelf local performance: F1 = 0.68 for SR and 0.52 for AF.
links.quote: Off-the-shelf model showed limited transferability (F1 = 0.68 for sinus rhythm (SR), 0.52 for atrial fibrillation (AF)).

links.outcome: fine-tuning with local weak labels
links.effect: Amsterdam UMC Expert F1 improved AF 0.814 to 0.830 and SR 0.914 to 0.920; precision decreased AF –0.012, SR –0.014.
links.quote: Adding weakly labelled in-house data further improved recall and overall F1 scores, with only modest reductions in precision (AF –0.012, SR –0.014; Table 3 ).

links.outcome: reference-label annotator agreement
links.effect: Pairwise kappa median was 0.60 for SR and 0.49 for AF.
links.quote: Pairwise kappa among annotators had a median of 0.60 for SR and 0.49 for AF.

links.outcome: robustness to temporal windows and lead variation
links.effect: Second-half F1 changes vs first-half: Pub AF –0.015, SR –0.006; Pub+weak AF –0.000, SR –0.004.
links.quote: Performance was stable across temporal windows, with slightly greater–but still modest–variability across lead configurations, likely influenced by the imbalance between the 1–4 and 5–8 lead groups (Appendix Tables 13 – 14 ).

links.outcome: arrhythmia classification F1 score on local ICU data
links.effect: Off-the-shelf ECG-FM showed limited transferability on local ICU data, achieving an F1 of 0.52 for atrial fibrillation and 0.68 for sinus rhythm.
links.quote: Off-the-shelf model showed limited transferability (F1 = 0.68 for sinus rhythm (SR), 0.52 for atrial fibrillation (AF)).

links.outcome: arrhythmia classification recall and F1 score on local ICU data
links.effect: Adding weakly labelled in-house data improved AF F1 from 0.814 to 0.830 and SR F1 from 0.914 to 0.920, with modest precision reductions of 0.012 (AF) and 0.014 (SR).
links.quote: Adding weakly labelled in-house data further improved recall and overall F1 scores, with only modest reductions in precision (AF –0.012, SR –0.014; Table 3 ).

screen.practice: local fine-tuning and validation on local ICU data before deployment
screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of off-the-shelf versus locally fine-tuned ECG foundation models on ICU patient monitoring data, assessing the transferability and need for local validation and fine-tuning.

primary.practice: local validation and fine-tuning before deployment
